rationale: The workflow has four Windows build jobs with no job-level timeout, so a hung or runaway build can consume the full default runner duration. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the pattern catalogue and by experiment records batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 and batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8, which added timeout-minutes to jobs and reported reduced runaway consumption. Adding timeout-minutes: 30 to each job is a minimal, workflow-scoped change that preserves all four build jobs, all compile steps, and all artifact uploads unchanged. It does not alter permissions, add secrets, introduce network access, or add publishing/deployment operations. The 30-minute budget provides operational headroom for MSVC compilation and artifact upload while bounding runaway consumption; false timeout failures should be monitored separately as the pattern advises.
